## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Preserve tracked fingerprints during refresh before merging. Refreshing after adding a file can erase the evidence verification needs to detect a hand edit.

## Changes

The pull request adds functions to refresh manifest fingerprints and register unlisted files. It adds tests for both functions.

## Critical

- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Preserve tracked fingerprints during refresh — Refreshing `["tracked.txt", "new.txt"]` after a hand edit to `tracked.txt` replaces its original digest. The assignment overwrites the baseline that `verify` uses to detect the edit. — When a user adds a file and refreshes the manifest, verification can accept a hand-edited tracked file as intact. — Fix: Reuse `register_new_files` to add only names absent from the manifest.

## Important

- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Normalize relative Path inputs before storing keys — Passing `[Path("new.txt")]` to either helper raises `TypeError` for an existing file. Both helpers store the `Path` as a dictionary key, which `json.dumps` rejects. — Callers passing relative `Path` objects cannot register their files. — Fix: Convert each supplied path to a string before looking it up or storing it.
- app/integrity.py:25 — correctness — Exclude the manifest from fingerprint updates — When a root-wide scan passes an unlisted `fingerprints.json` to either helper and that file is the manifest, verification fails immediately after the update. Both helpers hash the manifest before rewriting it to include its own digest. — Users who include the manifest in a bulk update get a verification failure even when their content files are intact. — Fix: Skip any candidate that resolves to the manifest file before hashing it.

## Suggestions

- PR body — correctness — Describe refresh as a Python function — A reader trying to use the advertised “refresh command” has no shell entry point to invoke. The pull request exposes refresh through the importable `refresh_fingerprints` function. — Users automating refresh from a shell need to supply their own Python invocation.
